constraints.subject: homeassistant.components.*
constraints.justification: ADR-0004: 'We no longer accept any new integration that relies on webscraping', with the Context naming 'PhantomJS or other headless browsers' as webscraping mechanisms; selenium (browser automation for scraping) is reliance on webscraping inside a core integration, and neither exception clause (generic HTML-parsing integrations; extracting fields from forms during authentication) covers browser automation

note: Constraint evidence (webscraping ban, headless-browser arm): ADR-0004 Proposal line 1 bans webscraping-reliant integrations; Context bullet 3 names headless browsers as a webscraping mechanism; at the pin zero selenium imports exist anywhere under homeassistant/ (grep 'from selenium|import selenium' empty), so the constraint baseline is clean. Object is the bare top-level import target 'selenium' (IMPORTS edge targets record the literal dotted import); exact object 'gpiozero'-style prefix rule also catches deep targets like selenium.webdriver via the startswith(object + '.') reachability check. Deliberately NOT encoded: (a) 'homeassistant.components.* prohibits bs4' — the Exceptions section carves out generic HTML-parsing integrations, and scrape IS that sanctioned generic integration (homeassistant/components/scrape/coordinator.py:7 'from bs4 import BeautifulSoup', manifest requirements beautifulsoup4==4.13.3), so a bs4 prohibition false-positives on the ADR's own exception at baseline; the pattern grammar (exact or prefix.* only, no negation) cannot express 'all components except scrape', so the bs4 arm is dropped rather than encoded dirty. (b) The auth-phase exception ('An integration is allowed to extract fields from forms') is narrower than selenium automation; any auth-phase selenium usage surfacing later is a dismissal-review case, not a gold change. Custom integrations are outside the subject (they do not live under homeassistant.components).*

Deliberately NOT encoded: 'Integrations that are discoverable must provide a unique id (via async_set_unique_id)'. The mandate applies only to discoverable integrations' discovery steps — an inexpressible subject restriction (pattern grammar has no way to select 'integrations whose config_flow does discovery'); encoding 'homeassistant.components.*.config_flow requires async_set_unique_id' would fire on every changed FQN in every config_flow module that does not call async_set_unique_id in that change, manufacturing a mandate the ADR scopes to discovery flows (the openlobby class-A over-trigger failure mode at benchmark scale: ~2000 config_flow modules). Call-shaped and exception-heavy per the census preview; revisit only if a call-predicate with subject restriction lands in the ontology (docs/adr/004). Emit no edges.

constraints.subject: homeassistant.components.*
constraints.justification: ADR-0019: 'We no longer accept integrations that integrate with devices over GPIO' and 'We identify, deprecate and remove integrations that use GPIO'; gpiozero is the GPIO access library, so a core integration importing it is a GPIO integration pending removal, and only custom integrations (outside homeassistant.components) may keep using GPIO

note: Constraint evidence (GPIO ban, gpiozero arm): ADR-0019 Decision bullets 1-3; at the pin the only gpiozero consumer in the tree is the legacy remote_rpi_gpio integration — module-level 'from gpiozero import LED, DigitalInputDevice' (homeassistant/components/remote_rpi_gpio/__init__.py:3), 'from gpiozero.pins.pigpio import PiGPIOFactory' (homeassistant/components/remote_rpi_gpio/__init__.py:4), 'from gpiozero import DigitalInputDevice' (binary_sensor.py:5), 'from gpiozero import LED' (switch.py:5); manifest quality_scale 'legacy', requirements gpiozero==1.6.2 + pigpio==1.78, codeowners empty — exactly the deprecate-and-remove state the ADR mandates, so the constraint has a GENUINE live violation at the pin (module-level dedup collapses the three files into one report at the package module homeassistant.components.remote_rpi_gpio). Object is the exact bare 'gpiozero' import target: the reachability check's startswith(object + '.') rule also catches the deep edge target gpiozero.pins.pigpio, so no gpiozero.* wildcard is needed (a wildcard object pattern would orphan: the object NODE bucket would need a node strictly under gpiozero.*, which merge_constraint_edges does not create). Scope notes: no RPi.GPIO-proper, spidev, or smbus2 imports exist at the pin (greps empty), so those arms are not encoded (never-fire family); the serial-device exemption needs no encoding because exempted integrations use pyserial, not gpiozero. Reading addressed: the Definition sentence qualifies GPIO as pins 'on the board running Home Assistant' while remote_rpi_gpio drives a remote Pi's pins via the pigpio daemon — under the Decision's unqualified removal mandate ('integrations that use GPIO') and the exemption list (only serial-exposed devices), remote_rpi_gpio remains a violation; flagged for the delayed blind self-review.

Interpreter-floor policy ('supports a single minor version of Python at a time'), superseding ADR-0002 (the pair counts once as natural conflict #2). Same non-encodable family as ADR-0002: no interpreter version is named as rejected, and version floors live in the version-check code, not in dependency edges. Only one of the supersession pair could ever be active; neither encodes. Emit no edges.
Deprecation-period process for YAML integration configuration (how long old config shapes stay supported). Process policy, not code structure. Emit no edges.
Grading framework (the quality scale itself: internal/gold/platinum). A rubric, not a code relation; quality_scale values in manifests are metadata, not FQN edges. Emit no edges.
